A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable, and corresponding content can be matched across the reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original numerical convergence experiments and Wasserstein GAN experiments on Gaussian data and MNIST digit 0 (Figures 2–3 and Table 2).

after.justification: v2 retains original numerical and GAN experiments and adds Fashion-MNIST results and computational-time comparisons (Table 3 and Figure 4).

M1.justification: The τ-GDA, full and asymptotic τ-SGA updates, stochastic adjustment using independent minibatches, and GAN architectures are retained. The expanded convergence analysis concerns existing procedures.

E1.justification: v2 adds Fashion-MNIST restricted to the T-shirt class, using the existing GAN architecture (Appendix L.6). The numerical example, Gaussian modeling task, and MNIST digit-0 coverage remain.

E2.justification: Both versions compare τ-GDA with τ-SGA and compare full with asymptotic τ-SGA in the numerical example. The added Fashion-MNIST and timing comparisons use the existing GDA/SGA comparator pair.

E3.justification: The numerical example replaces the unstable τ-GDA setting τ=10 with τ=30. New Figure 4 evaluates objective/test FID against wall-clock time, selecting configurations by objective or validation FID and specifying separate learning rates. The existing MNIST Table 2 protocol is unchanged.

E4.justification: v1 reports only a per-iteration overhead estimate. v2 adds a substantive computational-efficiency analysis across the numerical example, MNIST, and Fashion-MNIST (Appendix K.2, Figure 4), testing whether convergence advantages survive the additional computation cost. Existing sensitivity and full/asymptotic comparisons remain.

E5.justification: Both retain ten resamplings of generated samples for estimating GAN quantities and the same standard-deviation/significant-digit reporting convention. Table 3 extends that convention; no new training-seed protocol, repeated-training-run analysis, or significance testing is reported.

E6.justification: v2 adds Fashion-MNIST results and wall-clock convergence curves. Table 3 reports validation FID 38.7±0.5 for τ-GDA at 200,000 iterations and 33.3±0.3 for τ-SGA at 3 million iterations, under unequal budgets. Gaussian trajectories are replaced despite unchanged stated settings, and the numerical divergence example changes to τ=30. MNIST Table 2 values remain identical.

T1.justification: v2 adds explicit Riemannian linear-rate guarantees, revises Theorem 3.1's fixed-point and regularity conditions, and adds rate bounds and supporting arguments in Appendices G.2 and J.2. It also changes the step-size bound's denominator from |λ|² in v1 Appendix G to |λ| in Section 3.2, compromising the general convergence guarantees as printed.

C1.justification: v1 foregrounds extending DSE/DNE definitions to manifolds and establishing local convergence. v2 treats these definitions as background and foregrounds explicit linear convergence rates and conditional rate improvements from τ-SGA. This substantially changes the contributions emphasized in the abstract, introduction, and conclusion.

C2.justification: v2 adds an interpretation of orthogonal adjustment through compatibility with potential/Hamiltonian dynamics and qualifies practical speedup through computational overhead. Its conclusion newly suggests DSE as a suitable solution concept for GAN training. The stochastic-theory and non-asymptotic-analysis limitations were already acknowledged in v1.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly specifies k=d=5 for the Gaussian discriminator, explains the absence of batch normalization in the MNIST generator, documents added experimental configurations, and announces a future PyTorch release. Existing architecture, retraction, and pretraining details are retained; the release announcement does not establish available code.

R1.justification: v2 newly attributes manifold DNE to Ratliff et al. (2013), distinguishes it from Kristály (2014), and repositions equilibrium definitions as background rather than a main novelty. Additional references and comparisons address GAN generalization, two-timescale training, and the relationship of the new rate bounds to Li et al. (2022).

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, theoretical exposition, and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting. v2 adds explicit contribution and notation blocks, reorders the equilibrium definitions, moves the main convergence proof into the appendix, reorganizes appendices, and changes terminology from differentiable to differential equilibrium.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document template and heading style, restructures Table 1, moves the convergence diagram from main-text Figure 1 to appendix Figure 3, revises the numerical example's first panel and axes, and adds the three-panel timing Figure 4 and Fashion-MNIST Table 3.

improvement.justification: The expanded rate analysis, clearer attribution, and wall-clock validation provide substantial benefits. However, v2 drops the square from the step-size bound's denominator (Section 3.2 versus v1 Appendix G), permitting step sizes inconsistent with spectral stability and undermining Theorems 3.2–3.4 as printed. These gains coexist with a correctness regression in central guarantees, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
